turns.learner: Hello teacher! I want to practise talking about things around me, like my room and my house.
turns.tutor:
Hello! Good topic. Today we use a, an and the with things around us.

Example: I have a dog. The dog is brown.

We use a the first time. Then we use the.

Now you try. Write one sentence about a thing in your house. Start with: I have...

turns.learner: I have a table in my room. A table is big and brown.
turns.tutor:
Good: "I have a table in my room." That sentence is clear.

Now look at your second sentence: "A table is big and brown." Check the first word again.

Write the second sentence again.

turns.learner: A table is big and brown. I think it is correct, teacher?
turns.tutor:
Not yet. "A table" is right in your first sentence. But in your second sentence, the table is already in your story.

Look at the first word of the second sentence one more time. Write it again.

turns.learner: I don't understand. It is a table, so I write a table. Is the first word wrong?
turns.tutor:
The first word is wrong only in the second sentence. In the first sentence, "a table" is right.

Look at the course example: "I have a dog. The dog is brown." The first word of the second sentence is different.

Now change only the first word in your second sentence.

turns.learner: The table is big and brown. I copy the dog example, but I am not sure why.
turns.tutor:
Good: "The table is big and brown." The reason is that we already talked about the table, so it is not new.

First time: "I have a table in my room."
Second time: "The table is big and brown."

Tell me the rule in your own words.

turns.learner: First time I use a, and the second time I use the. Because we know the thing already.
turns.tutor:
Remember: use a the first time, and the when we already know the thing.

Now try this one.

Write a or an: I see ___ ant on the table.

Tell me the rule in your own words.

turns.learner: I see a ant on the table. I think a is correct because it is the first time.
turns.tutor:
You are right that this is the first time, so you use a or an, not the. But a and an are different: we use an before a vowel sound, like in "an egg". We use a before other sounds, like in "a dog".

Recap:
First time: a or an.
Second time: the.

Tell me the rule in your own words.
